- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

<text>
# Summary of Policy Document

This document outlines a comprehensive policy platform addressing multiple areas of governance, public services, and economic reform.

## Immigration and Border Control

The platform proposes freezing non-essential immigration while maintaining exceptions for healthcare workers. It advocates for offshore processing of asylum seekers, immediate deportation of foreign nationals who commit crimes, restrictions on student dependents, and a five-year residency requirement before accessing benefits. An employer tax of 20% on foreign workers is proposed to incentivise hiring domestic workers, with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses.

## Economic Policy

**Personal taxation** proposals include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 annually, reducing stamp duty, abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and cutting energy taxes. **Business measures** include raising the corporation tax threshold, reducing the main rate from 25% to 15% over time, lifting the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolishing business rates for high street enterprises, and introducing an online delivery tax for large multinationals.

## Government Spending

The document proposes saving £50 billion annually through departmental efficiency measures, ending interest payments to commercial banks on quantitative easing reserves (estimated £35 billion savings), and cutting foreign aid by 50%. It advocates scrapping retained EU regulations and improving tax collection.

## Healthcare

Proposals include tax exemptions for frontline NHS staff, removing training caps for medical students, offering 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and introducing a voucher scheme allowing patients to access private treatment if NHS waiting times exceed specified limits. Weekend operating theatre availability and pharmacy-first initiatives are also proposed.

## Energy and Environment

The platform advocates abandoning net zero targets and associated subsidies, fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licensing, exploring shale gas extraction, and developing nuclear power through small modular reactors. This is projected to save households £500 annually.

## Law Enforcement and Justice

Proposals include recruiting 40,000 additional police officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing, mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, building 10,000 new detention places, and reopening magistrates' courts. Changes to hate crime definitions and child grooming penalties are also proposed.

## Education

The platform proposes curriculum changes emphasising national heritage, prohibiting gender identity teaching in schools, offering 20% tax relief on independent education, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers while enforcing minimum entry standards.

## Benefits System

Proposals include a two-strike rule requiring benefit recipients to accept employment within four months or after two job offers, face-to-face assessments for disability benefits, and using the raised income tax threshold as an incentive to work.

## Defence

The document proposes increasing defence spending to 3% of GDP within six years, introducing pay reviews for armed forces personnel, creating a dedicated veterans department, and recruiting 30,000 full-time army personnel rather than implementing national service.

## Housing and Infrastructure

Proposals include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping certain landlord tax restrictions, and cancelling a major rail project. The platform opposes urban emission zones and low-traffic neighbourhoods.

## Agriculture and Fishing

The farming budget would increase to £3 billion with focus on smaller farms, while climate-related subsidies would be scrapped. Fishing proposals include ending automatic EU access to UK waters, requiring foreign vessels to purchase licences, and banning supertrawlers.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposals include withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights, reforming the upper legislative chamber, changing postal voting rules, and considering proportional representation through referendum.

## Financial Summary

The document claims potential annual savings of £150 billion through spending cuts and efficiency measures, plus £10 billion from projected economic growth. Proposed spending increases total £141 billion annually, covering tax cuts, healthcare, defence, policing, and other areas.
